assessment_summary:
I reviewed DEPLOYMENT.md and the installation summary, then inspected the resulting environment and exercised the built artifacts directly.

Scope verified: `git log` confirms commit 520d93f at /workspace; `docker images` shows 29 project images plus the public base images named in the guide. The guide's documented non-Docker frontend route (`npm ci && npm run build:all`) produced the 9 expected workspace dist outputs; I served the shell dist via nginx and confirmed HTTP 200 on `/` and a favicon, so the frontend build is functional. I also confirmed the demospipes images exist with the tags given in the summary.

Operational checks: I started built images and probed live endpoints. xoev-adapter, tex2pdf-service (health endpoint 200, container healthy), dokumentensuche, nachforderungen, and demospipes-addon-bmds-api (after supplying its required env) all served HTTP 200 with valid OpenAPI/health responses. This demonstrates many images are genuinely runnable, not just present.

Failures that establish the outcome: running fristenmanagement and decision-log-store-service yields exit code 1 with `ImportError ... greenlet library is installed`. SQLAlchemy's dist-info declares greenlet only under the `asyncio` extra; the venv lacks greenlet and the generated fristenmanagement/uv.lock contains zero greenlet references — a build-time dependency-resolution defect. These services crash at import, before reading any runtime configuration, so no environment variable can make them work. Separately, rechtsquellenvorbereitung exits 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mistralai.utils'`: the image ships mistralai 3.1.0, which does not expose that submodule, while the source imports it — an incompatible/unpinned dependency resolved during the build.

I distinguished these from the many services that exit solely because their runtime dependencies (PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Neo4j, LLM endpoints, env vars) are absent. Those failures are expected under the guide and are not treated as installation failures. Limitations: some services could not be brought fully up without the guided external infrastructure; the frontend `mfe-ewm` was not built, but it is not part of the documented `build:all` target, so that alone is not conclusive. The Docker/Podman socket dropped transiently mid-session and recovered; all reported results were captured after recovery. I made no repairs or edits.

Net: the frontend and several backend services are operational, but multiple backend service images are non-functional due to broken dependency resolution. The installation is therefore incomplete and cannot operate without further repair, meeting the definition of failure.
